newsitem.title: USA: Guyanor pleased with drilling results.
newsitem.headline: Guyanor pleased with drilling results.

text.p: Golden Star Resources Ltd said 68 percent owned Guyanor Ressources SA is pleased with core drilling results from the contiguous St-Elie and Dieu-Merci projects in French Guiana.
The 99 square kilometer St-Elie property and 155 square kilometer Dieu-Merci property are being explored by Guyanor and ASARCO Inc through jointly owned Societe des Mines de St-Elie.
The Dieu Merci project includes the Kerouani and Virgile prospects. The adjacent St-Elie project includes the Chemin de Fer and Michel targets.

Jean-Francois Sauvage, managing director of Guyanor, said, "We are particularly pleased with results of the drilling at Kerouani and Michel where we have successfully demonstrated the continuation of near surface mineralization into hard rock.

"At Kerouani, we clearly have the potential for multiple horizons of relatively flat-lying gold mineralization at depth. At Michel, the pervasive zone of alteration gives us good potential to build gold resources at depth. Kerouani remains open in all directions while Michel remains open along strike and at depth."
However, "at Virgile and Chemin de Fer we expected better showings at depth based upon near surface gold mineralization demonstrated through trenching or shallow drilling," Sauvage said.

"Based upon this information, Guyanor plans to focus on the evaluation of near surface potential through a program of systematic deep augering over the Chemin de Fer, Kerouani, Virgile, Cesar and Devis Sud targets. This work is intended to allow us to begin quantifying saprolite hosted gold resources at these targets while we continue core drilling the six targets on St-Elie/Dieu-Merci that remain to be tested at depth."
He also pointed out "other positive developments that have occurred in French Guiana," including budgeting to build a new road to open up the interior of the country beginning in 1998.
"At the same time, the authorities announced a significant reduction in local fuel taxes is seriously being considered for the mining industry in French Guiana."
